subject: Numeracy
title: First, second and third
objectives: Children will say first, second, third and last.
Children will describe the order of a line.
content: First and last, second and third, and race and queue games.
teachingActivities: Use real lines and races where children can see who is first; say "first, second, third" aloud; distinguish counting numbers (one, two) from ordinal numbers (first, second); make sure every child gets a turn to be first.
learnerActivities: Say first, second, third and last and describe the order of a line.
resources: Ribbons or medals made of card
assessment: Observe whether each child says first and last and second and third with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says first and last in a line.
Says second and third with support.

lessons.title: First and last
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say who is first and who is last in a line.
successCriteria: Points to the first and last child
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use time words and order numbers.
lessons.starter: Make a line of children and say "Who is first? Who is last?"
teacherActivities: Show the first and last child in the line.
Change the order and ask again.
Let each child be first once.
learnerActivities: Children look and say first and last.
Child points to first and last.
Child points to the last child.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the first and last child in the line. Children: Children look and say first and last.
Step 2. Teacher: Change the order and ask again. Children: Child points to first and last.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child be first once. Children: Child stands at the front.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Who is last?" Children: Child points to the last child.

practical.title: Line up
practical.safety: Keep the line safe and orderly and supervise movement. Make sure every child has a turn at the front.

differentiation.support: Make a line of three children.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to organise a line of five.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Points to the first and last child
lessons.conclusion: Walk in a line and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about who is first and last in family queues.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say who is first and who is last in a line" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Second and third
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say second and third and describe where someone is in a line.
successCriteria: Places an object in the correct position
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use time words and order numbers.
lessons.starter: Put three toy cars in a row and say "The red car is first. The blue car is second. The green car is third."
teacherActivities: Name the position of each car in the row.
Let children place cars in order.
learnerActivities: Child points to the second car.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Name the position of each car in the row. Children: Children say first, second, third.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which car is second?" Children: Child points to the second car.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children place cars in order. Children: Child places cars.
Step 4. Teacher: Match ordinal cards to cars. Children: Child matches a card.

practical.title: Car order
practical.safety: Use large toy cars and keep them off the floor after use. Supervise closely.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put five cars in order and name fourth and fifth.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which car is third?
questions.expected: The last car in the row.

expectedOutcomes: Places objects in the correct position
lessons.conclusion: Put the cars away and say first, second, third.
lessons.homeConnection: Say first, second and third when queueing at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say second and third and describe where someone is in a line" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Race game
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will take part in a race and say the finishing order.
successCriteria: Says who was first, second and third
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use time words and order numbers.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we have a walking race. We will see who is first, second and third."
teacherActivities: Explain the rules: walk, do not push.
Ring the bell and let small groups race.
Name the first, second and third.
Give each racer a medal or sticker.
learnerActivities: Children walk to the finish line.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Explain the rules: walk, do not push. Children: Children repeat walk.
Step 2. Teacher: Ring the bell and let small groups race. Children: Children walk to the finish line.
Step 3. Teacher: Name the first, second and third. Children: Children say the order.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each racer a medal or sticker. Children: Child receives a medal.

practical.title: Walking race
practical.safety: Make it a walking race with a clear track and no pushing. Supervise closely and make sure every child is celebrated.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the race judge.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Cheer for everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Have a walking race at home and say who is first.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "take part in a race and say the finishing order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Queue and order
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will describe the order of a queue and take turns in it.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use time words and order numbers.
resources: A pretend shop or bus stop
lessons.starter: Say "We are waiting at the shop. Who is first in the queue?"
teacherActivities: Make a queue at the pretend shop.
Say who is first, second and third.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make a queue at the pretend shop. Children: Children line up in order.
Step 2. Teacher: Say who is first, second and third. Children: Children say the order.
Step 3. Teacher: Serve the first customer. Children: Child buys and moves away.
Step 4. Teacher: Say who is first now. Children: Child says the new first.

practical.title: Shop queue
practical.safety: Supervise the queue closely and keep the area clear. Ensure every child gets a turn.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say where they are in the queue.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Tidy the shop and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about queues when you go out.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "describe the order of a queue and take turns in it" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 order check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses first, second, third and last.
successCriteria: Says second and third with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use time words and order numbers.
lessons.starter: Sing the first second third song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: cars, queue and race.
At each station ask "Who is second?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: cars, queue and race. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Who is second?" Children: Child answers and points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Order stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large cars only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use first and last only.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to use fourth and fifth.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says first and last; says second and third; describes a queue; takes turns in order.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep using first, second and third at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses first, second, third and last" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
